# Slack

Channels, messages, threads, users, files, reactions, pins, reminders, user groups, search and the rest of the Slack Web API (171 tools, 108 of them mutations; every mutation asks for approval).

**Interface:** OpenAPI. Source is Slack's official Swagger 2.0 description (version 1.7.0), `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slackapi/slack-api-specs/master/web-api/slack_web_openapi_v2.json`, published by the `slackapi` GitHub organisation on `master` (not pinned to a commit). The document is patched at load time and is not Slack's verbatim file: 19 schemas whose `items` is an array (invalid Swagger 2 tuple form) are replaced with a plain object schema, which otherwise causes core methods such as `chat.postMessage` and `conversations.list` to be skipped. The patches are in `openapi.ts`.

**Approvals:** Slack declares many side-effecting methods as GET (`views.open`, `views.publish`, `apps.uninstall`, `auth.revoke`, `dialog.open`, `files.remote.share`, `workflows.*` and others). These are forced to mutations with `kinds` so they ask for approval. Some read-only POST methods are also treated as mutations and so ask for approval; this is safe but noisy. The `oauth.access`, `oauth.token` and `oauth.v2.access` methods are removed because they take `client_secret` as a query parameter. Slack's official remote MCP server (`https://mcp.slack.com/mcp`) was probed but needs a directory-published or internal Slack app, so it is not usable for arbitrary users.

**Auth**

- Token: a bot token (`xoxb-`) or user token (`xoxp-`) from your Slack app's "OAuth & Permissions" page at https://api.slack.com/apps. This method keeps the supplied token as-is.
- User OAuth (`user`): create a Slack app at https://api.slack.com/apps, add the redirect URI shown on the host's connect page, add the scopes below under **User Token Scopes**, and enter the client ID and secret. This flow sends a comma-separated `user_scope` only; it omits the OAuth `scope` parameter and does not request a bot grant. The exchange requires `authed_user.access_token`, which is used for health checks and API calls.

  `user_scope` contains:

  - Conversations: `channels:history`, `channels:read`, `channels:write`, `groups:history`, `groups:read`, `groups:write`, `im:history`, `im:read`, `im:write`, `mpim:history`, `mpim:read`, `mpim:write`.
  - Messages and search: `chat:write`, `links:write`, `reactions:read`, `reactions:write`, `search:read`.
  - Files: `files:read`, `files:write`, `remote_files:read`, `remote_files:share`.
  - Calls and presence: `calls:read`, `calls:write`, `dnd:read`, `dnd:write`, `users:write`.
  - Pins, reminders and workspace data: `emoji:read`, `pins:read`, `pins:write`, `reminders:read`, `reminders:write`, `team:read`, `usergroups:read`, `usergroups:write`, `users.profile:read`, `users.profile:write`, `users:read`, `users:read.email`.


**Known gaps**

- No operations are skipped after the patches (171 of the 174 spec operations are exposed; the 3 removed are the oauth.* methods above).
- The OpenAPI router exposes 171 methods. Admin methods still need admin scopes, and methods whose Slack documentation requires a bot or app-level token cannot use this user grant.
- [`files.remote.add`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/files.remote.add/), [`files.remote.remove`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/files.remote.remove/), and [`files.remote.update`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/files.remote.update/) require `remote_files:write`. Slack documents that scope as bot-token-only and says remote files must be added by bots, not individual users. The user grant includes `remote_files:read` and `remote_files:share`, but not these writes.
- Slack's [`stars.add`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/stars.add/), [`stars.list`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/stars.list/), and [`stars.remove`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/stars.remove/) methods still accept user scopes, but current docs say users can no longer view or interact with saved items through these APIs and recommend retiring app functionality that relies on them. The user grant does not request `stars:read` or `stars:write`.
- Slack rejects `tokens.basic` as an illegal user scope during app registration. The user grant omits it.
- [`users.identity`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/users.identity/) requires Slack identity scopes, which this grant intentionally omits.
- The user grant omits `bookmarks:*` and `canvases:*` because the maintained OpenAPI description contains no corresponding operations.
- File uploads via the legacy multipart `files.upload` are not supported.
- Icon is Slack's hash mark from the Slack website (`a.slack-edge.com`), as Simple Icons has no Slack entry.
